messages.author: d994cff5897faec8
messages.subject: Completely remove the legend?
parts:
A few times now I've found myself wanting to completely remove the
legend on a plot. I can get rid of most of it by setting legend
properties to theme_blank() with opts(), but the indicators themselves
remain, and it's terribly verbose, anyway. Is there a good way to do
this?

I would also like to be able to remove the tickmarks on one axis
without also removing them from the other axis, and to be able to
remove all of the label on one axis (title, text, and ticks) in one go
-- again, the opts() approach gets awfully verbose.

Thanks,
zw

messages.subject: Re: Completely remove the legend?
parts:
forgot about the second paragraph...

you can do all that stuff and save it to a theme that you can then
stick in-line and not have to "repeat yourself". I think you're going
to have to be verbose to get what you want esp if its significantly
different from the default, at least ggplot provides a way to save it
all in a theme.

print out theme_bw() and you'll see all of the attributes you were
talking about. you could just put those straight into another them or
copy such a preexisting theme altering the few details you want
changed.

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Completely remove the legend?
parts:
> There were two things in the second paragraph.  I have found no way at
> all to suppress ticks on one of the axes but not the other.

+ scale_x_continuous(breaks = NA) should do it.

Unfortunately you'd then have to add the grid lines back in with
geom_vline/geom_hline.
